speaker: @AlpacaAurelius
quote: negative thinking destroys your brain. being a silly goose and delusionally optimistic is the ultimate longevity hack
cited: Ye et al., BMC Psychiatry 2025: Repetitive negative thinking is associated with cognitive function decline in older adults: a cross-sectional study
verdict: The paper reports a cross-sectional association between repetitive negative thinking and lower MoCA scores in older adults in Wuhan; the post turns it into a causal claim that it destroys the brain in everyone.
found: 424 adults aged 60+, single site, one survey. Top vs bottom quartile of repetitive negative thinking: about 1.6 MoCA points lower. Association absent at ages 80 to 90 and in the least educated.
beyond: Delusional optimism as a longevity hack: the cited paper measured neither optimism nor longevity.

audit.label: The paper's own citations (50 statement-reference pairs)
audit.note: The paper's claim that negative thinking 'depletes the brain's limited resources' cites an eye-tracking experiment on attention, not a study of decline.

speaker: Labroots
quote: Researchers suggest avoiding very high coffee intake (five or more cups a day)
cited: INTERSTROKE case-control study, 32 countries (13,462 cases, 13,488 controls)
verdict: The paper is a case-control study with a borderline adjusted OR of 1.37 (1.06 to 1.77) for more than 4 cups a day; the article generalizes to everyone and gives no magnitude or uncertainty.
found: Coffee more than 4 cups/day vs none: adjusted OR 1.37 (95% CI 1.06 to 1.77) for all stroke. Case-control design.

speaker: Hindustan Times
quote: coffee in these dosages decreases the risk of heart disease, stroke, heart failure, type 2 diabetes, and, interestingly, even atrial fibrillation
cited: American Heart Association scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular health
verdict: The statement calls most of the evidence observational, the diabetes data inconsistent, and gives no 2 to 4 cup dose; the article states five benefits as settled.
found: Mostly observational evidence: lower type 2 diabetes risk, lower stroke risk at moderate intake, heart failure 'no relationship or' lower risk; the one AF trial is paired with more premature ventricular contractions.
graph: Graph check, coffee and cardiovascular disease: 10 studies, 10 independent sources; headline directions 4 lower, 4 null, 1 higher.

speaker: Diabetes.co.uk
quote: reduce their mortality risk by 22% compared to those who do not drink tea or coffee
cited: UK Biobank prospective cohort, joint coffee and tea categories
verdict: Causal wording for an observational cohort; the 22% figure is not in the extracted record.
found: Prospective cohort with a 16-group joint coffee-tea model versus neither beverage; self-reported intake from one baseline question.
fields: two to four cups of tea and under one to two of coffee
